source.access: Entwine Point Tiles, public usgs-lidar-public bucket (AWS Open Data), anonymous HTTPS, octree depth <= 10
source.flightDatesNote: FGDC metadata (begdate/enddate) of the delivery tile at the Evanston test area, read in the Phase 5B pilot. The Lakeview tile's own metadata was not read; same delivery, so the same flight window is assumed (unverified for that tile).
source.points: vendor building class (6) at least 2 m above a 5 m ground grid (classification) / 1 m (heights); about 4 points per m2 of roof

header.licenceNote: AWS Open Data registry lists the dataset as US Government Public Domain; the USGS copyright page itself was blocked (403) in the pilot, so the wording is unverified at the source. Acknowledgement of the originating agencies is requested in derived products (FGDC useconst).

footprints.note: closed building ways and building multipolygons whose centroid is inside the area; keys are OSM refs (way/<id>, relation/<id>)

handCheck.fourClassAccuracy: 24 of 30 (80 %; flat/gable/hip/complex; the complex class over-calls: 6 of 18 simple roofs read complex)

mansard.comment: Hand check of the mansard rule (roofhints.mansard_rule), 2026-10-06. Aggregates only; no refs or images committed. Roofs were viewed as scratch point-cloud height surfaces (facet colours) with two side views, the same style as the pilot's hand check, and judged by the agent from the same points the rule used (a check of the rule's reading, not ground truth).
mansard.selection: Not a random sample: the one roof the first rule version flagged, the highest-scoring near misses (steep share of significant plane area) in both areas (16), and the 4 roofs a looser steep threshold (42 deg) would flag. Evanston South 12, Lakeview 9.

firstRuleVersion.note: the one flagged roof was a flat roof with a steep gable strip across the middle (two steep sides only)

finalRule.flaggedNote: a flat-topped roof with four 45 deg sides (a truncated hip / deck roof): a steep ring round a flat top as the rule defines it, but not a classic 60-80 deg mansard
finalRule.rejectedNote: gables, hips and cross-gables with steep (45-55 deg) planes; three of the four loose-threshold candidates were cross-gable complex roofs

findings: Planes of 50 deg or more are rare: 92 of 10,753 planes of at least 4 m2 (0.9 %) in the two areas, and none forms a ring round a flat or low top. No classic steep mansard was found in either area; about 45 deg (12:12) is the dominant steep slope.

Thresholds (steepMinPitch 45, ringMinShare 0.95, maxSteepPlanes 5) were set on these same roofs after the first version failed, so 1 of 1 and 20 of 20 are not an independent accuracy estimate. Recall cannot be estimated: no independent set of true mansards exists in the two areas.

handCheck.scope: the accuracy figures come from South Evanston (houses and garages); the classifier was not hand-checked on Chicago flat-roofed courtyard and multi-unit buildings (Lakeview) - unverified there

header.pitchClasses: flat < 10 deg; low 10 to < 25; medium 25 to 40; steep > 40 (pitchDeg = dominant plane slope)

fields.topM: roof top above ground, m (95th percentile of building points, ground = median class-2 ring 3 to 8 m around the footprint)
fields.eaveM: eave height above ground, m (15th percentile of points within 0.5 to 2 m of the footprint edge); null when too few points
fields.pitchDeg: slope of the dominant plane, degrees; mansard = mean slope of the steep lower planes
fields.points: building-class lidar points inside the footprint eroded by 0.75 m
fields.confidence: heuristic 0-1 score (point cover, density, plane coverage, form factor); not a probability
